reviews.comment: He seemed nice but was stuck in online lectures all year due to his health. The lectures were pretty boring but he provided a lot of material to look over like slides and videos. I would have liked the class a lot more if it was not online lectures but other than that, not too bad.
mid.

reviews.comment: Super nice guy and very approachable. His lectures are not the greatest and can be mundane. Where he is really helpful is the amount of material he provides including the slides that he uploads on canvas or the Github which he keeps updated with code covering current topics and exam material.

BEST SLIDES of all professors for CS 121! His slides are the only reason I'm getting through this class with an A. All teachers give a common exam, so you can't blame him for exam/homework/lab content

I feel bad writing this review because I really liked his jokes that he told during class, but listening to his lectures at 8 am almost had me asleep towards the end of the semester. To be honest, the material in this class is very easy to learn on your own.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: McGuire isn't the best instructor for this course in terms of explaining the material. However, between the textbook, posted lecture slides, code examples, and access to other professor's resources, you never even need to show up. He requires no in-class work. If you're confident in your ability to learn independently and want less work, it's good.

This class is an A if you put in a little effort. Plenty of opportunities for extra credit and fair deadlines for assignments. Understanding prof when work starts piling up and is willing to work with you. Although grading took a long time , and reading off slides is something too. I left this class with tons of knowledge and got me more interested

This class was... interesting. I have never coded before, and honestly still don't really know how to. I feel like this may have been better in person, but that does not change the fact that I STILL DON'T KNOW MY GRADE and haven't known the whole semester. Midterm took 2 months to be graded and labs took awhile for grading. Labs weren't too hard.
He's a cool guy with a sense of humor. Lecture was boring but all the notes he goes over are posted online and really help with the labs. Labs were not too hard for the most part.
He is very bad at communicating and grading. It was immensely frustrating to be in his class. Nice guy, bad prof. Going into finals week with only two grades.

McGuire is disorganized. From not having submission boxes to not having them accept late work (despite having a late policy). He is also hard to reach; he never responds to emails nor to his own forum. The only reason I understand anything in this class is because of outside research. I'd give this prof zero out of five if it were possible.

Pros -Some extra credit here and there -Not as many quizzes as other professors -Review for every test/quiz Cons -Sometimes did not provide answers to reviews -Very bad lecturer reads straight from the slides no extra explanation -Tests cover material that was never mentioned/went over -Never responds to emails -Will not elaborate on practice probs

Dr. McGuire really made this class non-stressful. Our exams were great - averaged 90. Homework was assigned about every other week, sometimes it was easy and sometimes not. His lecture slides were thorough enough I felt like I didn't have to grind the textbook. Good explanations in lecture. Plenty of quiz and exam reviews were provided.

Dr. McGuire made the transition from in person to online much easier on us. Many professors saw that assigning readings/homework/quizzes was much easier to do online and went way overboard. Dr. McGuire did not. He assigned just as much work as he would have in person and he even joined our GroupMe and listened to our feedback. He's awesome.

McGuire does not know how to teach, at least when it comes to this abstract material. This class is mostly theory and all he does is read from slides probably taken from an Ivy League 10 years ago. When asked questions, he tends to make you feel bad about yourself for not knowing. I mostly taught myself from YouTube.

He was the worst professor I've taken at A&M. He didn't teach much of anything, every class was him reading from the slides. He would answer questions about the material super well but he didn't seek to challenge his students with the programming assignments. He also posted ALL the coding assignment grades hours before the deadline.

Dr. McGuire and his TA didn't grade our labs and homework until a few hours before the grades were supposed to go to the Office of Registrar. I had no idea how I was doing in class until it was too late to do anything. If you want to learn NOTHING - take his class, otherwise avoid. Easy to get an A, but no coding knowledge behind the grade.

It's a toss-up. The first time I took 222 with Lee and I Q drop because her class was pretty difficult. For Dr. Mcguire, I hardly showed up to class and got an A, but learned far less than I did with Lee. So if you want a better chance at an A, take Dr. McGuire, if you want to learn more, take someone else. He's a nice guy, but wasn't prepared.

Teaches material well and has a small workload. Projects are assigned 3 weeks before the due date and don't take more than an hour or 2 to code. Lectures are posted online for easy studying as well as providing a clear exam review for which concepts are going to be tested. If you have prior coding knowledge, this class is an easy A.
